newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore seeks laughter and light at WTO meeting.
newsitem.headline: Singapore seeks laughter and light at WTO meeting.

text.p: Singapore is even changing light bulbs in its quest to ensure that the inaugural Ministerial Conference of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) proceeds smoothly.

In keeping with its reputation for efficiency, the city-state's convention centre is replacing each of the more than 10,000 bulbs in the Singapore International Convention & Exhibition Centre (SICEC).

Given the island state's penchant for campaigns, it is not surprising that the centre is coming up with its own strategy to reinforce the government's S$2 million "Smile, Singapore" national campaign.

The centre will deploy more than 1,000 staff around the clock to provide "first-class service", and another 1,000 volunteers from the goverment will be mobilised as liaison officers, drivers and security staff.
An extra 65 km (40 miles) of cables and wiring have been added to cope with the expected extra demand for telecommunication services in the 10,000 sq metre (353,144 sq ft) building.
In addition, 4,700 wireless headsets, 800 microphones, 1,000 extra phone lines, and 38 extra women's toilets have been installed.

The government has allocated a Singapore $18 million budget for the conference, 40 percent of which will be spent on facilities. On top of this, the SICEC will spend S$6 million to spruce up the centre which was completed only 18 months ago.

David Chin, the chairman of the conference facility and programme committee said the steps were being taken "firstly, to ensure that conference facilities are comprehensive and will meet the high standards expected at such an international gathering, and secondly to ensure that delegates...will have a pleasant and memorable time".

Some roads around the central Marina area will be closed during the conference to clear the streets of traffic, but no special public holidays have been declared -- a method resorted to in Thailand for major international events.
Delegates and staff are being encouraged to use public transport to and from the the centre. Delegates will receive a complimentary stored-value ticket for the undergound railway.
